newsitem.title: USA: Kmart says can add $8 billion to $10 billion in sales.
newsitem.headline: Kmart says can add $8 billion to $10 billion in sales.

text.p: Kmart Corp., with years of cash flow problems finally behind it, on Tuesday outlined an ambitious plan for growth at its annual shareholders meeting.

Kmart said its 2,038 traditional stores have the potential to boost sales by $8 billion to $10 billion, or about three times its business last year. The company, the nation's third-largest retailer, had sales of more than $26 billion in 1996.

"We have the potential to grow our sales another $8 billion to $10 billion on this existing store base," Chairman Floyd Hall told shareholders. "That has encouraged us to refine and enthusiastically pursue the new store prototype -- which we call Big Kmart."

About 300 traditional Kmart stores have already been converted to the new prototype, which features design and other changes affecting 90 percent of the store. An additional 300 stores will be converted this year.

Kmart, based in Troy, Mich., is on track to modify as many as 450 stores into this format annually over the next three years, upgrading about half the chain and driving improved volumes, Hall said. The company will spend about $270 million to convert stores in 1997, he added.

"Our experience indicates that the store conversion process provides Kmart with improved performance against new competition, so our ongoing roll-out will emphasise metropolitan areas such as the Northeast, in which we anticipate increased competition over the next several years," Hall said in a presentation to shareholders.
He also said the retailer is in the early stages of a turnaround and must gain momentum that it can sustain.
"At the top of our agenda in 1997 is a tenacious push toward growing sales and improving profitability," Hall said.
He said the company plans to introduce a new Sesame Street line of clothing for infants, toddlers, boys and girls, as well as toys, books and related products this summer.

"You will see a powerful product launch for this new line which we believe will go a very long way in building our relationship with families who want the very best for their children at a price they can afford," Hall said.

He said Kmart is rolling out a new "co-branded" programme for its 850 in-store restaurants beginning this week. The new "KCafe" restaurants will have expanded menu offerings that feature national brands.

In the 530 Kmart stores that have a Little Caesars restaurant, the company will introduce a new format called "The KCafe/Little Caesars Pizza Station," offering a full new menu with freshly made pizza.
The 320 other restaurants will be called "The KCafe/Little Caesars Express."
The company said it plans to incorporate the new KCafe in all of its high-frequency Big Kmart stores.
Kmart's stock fell 12.5 cents to $14 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
